comment: Every place the document and the reference part company, and every place this model is deliberately not claiming something. Each entry says what the document says, what the reference does, which one this package follows, and what evidence would settle it.

sources.document: Nintendo SNES Development Manual, Book 1, the sound source chapters. Pinned in hardware.json.
sources.reference: snes9x 1.63 SPC_DSP.cpp, driven through conformance/ref and captured into corpus.json. An emulator, which is the lowest rung this family recognises and is evidence about that program rather than about the chip.

divergences.documentSays: Times and frequencies for the envelope and the noise clock, the register map, the BRR block format, and nothing at all about the sample values the chip produces.
divergences.referenceDoes: Produces sample values, which is what corpus.json records.
divergences.reasoning: The audio this model produces is checked against snes_spc 0.9.0, which is Shay Green's and is what snes9x carries. His spc_dsp6.sfc carries checks with values taken on a console, and run per check through the composed audio unit in sony-s-smp-python it reaches 104 verdicts, all of which agree (as of 2026-10-19). Seven used to disagree, from three causes each found in a second implementation at a pinned commit and confirmed by the console's value. The bent gain increase compared the previous hidden envelope with 0x600 as a signed number where snes_spc 0.9.0 and ares at 9408cb43 compare it unsigned. A write to OUTX or ENVX did not reach the value the schedule was holding to write there, which both implementations latch. And Misc/$F0-$FF are not ram was the audio unit's register file. The cartridge reaches sample values only through checksums of a few of them, so the rest of the audio still rests on agreement with snes_spc.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A recording of a real audio unit playing a known program, compared sample for sample. The cartridge, spc_dsp6.sfc with SHA-256 b12038f865536a33003c9887e6f86fcbcb526b7f1766526ab30cb74b7380aa9a from https://gitlab.com/higan/snes-test-roms at commit 26e8aa91e0d3b90b901e7e693bc4a8244b391d7b, is not carried here; cartridge.json records every verdict and how the run was driven.

divergences.documentSays: Table 3-7-2 gives a time for each decay rate "from 1 to SL" and for each sustain rate. It never says what level the measurement stops at, and "SL" cannot be the answer for the sustain column, which has no SL.
divergences.referenceDoes: Falls by one two hundred and fifty sixth per tick, which is the factor the manual itself prints. Dividing each of the 39 printed figures by this model's tick period for that rate gives 576 to 600 ticks, median 590: one endpoint, to within four per cent across the whole table.
divergences.reasoning: The tightness of that spread is the result worth having. It says the model's rate table reproduces every printed exponential figure exactly in relative terms, and that the only thing missing is a constant nobody wrote down. After 590 ticks this model's envelope stands at 105, about a nineteenth of full scale, which is not any of the eight sustain levels the manual defines. Rather than bend the model to land on a number the document never gives, the endpoint is recovered here and left where it is.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A measurement of a real S-DSP: key on a voice at a known decay rate, capture the envelope readback register, and see what level it holds when the printed time has elapsed.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing. Pitch is described as a fourteen bit value across P(L) and P(H) and the manual never gives the filter that resamples a decoded sample to it.
divergences.referenceDoes: Carries a 512 entry table, one quarter of a symmetric curve, which this model reproduces.
divergences.reasoning: This is the single largest thing in the model with no manufacturer source. It shapes every sample the chip emits, so an error in it is audible everywhere and is invisible to every check in hardware.test.py, which can only reach the tables the manual describes. A closed form was looked for on 2026-08-25 and none reproduces it. Fitted by least squares against the 512 entries, the best candidates leave a peak error of 18 on a maximum of 1305 for cos^3.5, 20 for a gaussian of sigma 0.63, and 38 for a cubic B-spline, against 380 for Catmull-Rom and 191 for cos^2. Nothing lands inside rounding, so the table is stored rather than computed and there is no derivation to publish in place of it.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A die photograph of the coefficient ROM, or a measurement: feed a known impulse at a known pitch and read the output back. A closed form would also have done it and does not exist; the search and its numbers are in the open questions so nobody repeats it.

divergences.documentSays: Nintendo documents the DSP as a licensee-facing register reference. It is not a Sony datasheet and does not describe the silicon.
divergences.reasoning: Nintendo shipped the part and wrote the manual its licensees programmed against, which makes this manufacturer documentation for the purpose. It is still one source, written to be programmed against rather than to describe a device.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A Sony S-DSP datasheet. Searched on 2026-08-21; nothing was found.

divergences.documentSays: Describes the DSP entirely in times and frequencies. It gives no cycle count anywhere, and the register map notes only that the DSP rewrites ENVX "at each Ts".
divergences.referenceDoes: Runs a sample at a time, in the order snes9x chose.
divergences.reasoning: Shay Green's spc_dsp6 carries an Order group and a Timing group whose names are the step numbers inside the thirty two step schedule, such as Timing/Misc/28 dir and Timing/Echo/22-23 echo read. All 19 Order checks and all 41 Timing checks agree with values taken on a console. The two Timing checks that used to disagree, V8 outx and V9 envx, were not an ordering finer than a step: a write to OUTX or ENVX did not reach the value the schedule was holding to write there. With the write latched, as snes_spc 0.9.0 and ares at 9408cb43 do, both agree. ares runs its schedule one step at a time as this model does, so no source here asks for a finer interval.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: Settled for what the cartridge reaches. A measurement of a real part reading a register inside a step would show whether anything finer exists.

divergences.documentSays: Nothing about what any register, counter, latch or voice holds at power on.
divergences.referenceDoes: Has no power on of its own: SPC_DSP::init runs its reset, so it starts from the state a reset sets.
divergences.reasoning: Nothing here begins cleared or reset. Every register, counter, latch, decoded sample and position holds a value drawn from a seed, across the values the model's logic gives that field, so a driver that depends on state it never set fails visibly rather than working by accident. The noise generator is drawn from everything but 0, the one value its feedback cannot leave, as powerOn in hardware.json records.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A capture of the register file, and of a voice keyed with noise on, on a real audio unit before anything is written to it, repeated across power cycles and across parts.

divergences.documentSays: That FLG carries a reset bit, and nothing about what a reset leaves in any register or latch.
divergences.referenceDoes: SPC_DSP::load and SPC_DSP::soft_reset_common clear every register and everything after them in the state block, set FLG to E0, each voice's block offset to 1, the noise to 4000 and the every-other-sample toggle to 1.
divergences.reasoning: The corpus agrees only while the reset does all of that: a reset that set the registers and released the voices and left the rest where power on put it agreed on 2 of the 240 cases. resetLine in hardware.json lists every field with its value and marks it unverified.
divergences.wouldSettleIt: A capture of the register file on a real audio unit immediately after reset, and of a voice keyed with noise on straight after it.

reference: snes_spc 0.9.0 by Shay Green, carried inside snes9x 1.63 at apu/bapu/dsp/SPC_DSP.cpp and driven through conformance/ref into corpus.json. Another implementation, which is the lowest rung this family recognises. Naming its author rather than the emulator around it cuts both ways: it is stronger than a generic emulator, and it is not independent of that author's hardware test programs, so agreeing with both is one judgement rather than two.
